name: Rufous-gaped Hillstar
rangeDescription: Andes of southwestern colombia and northwestern ecuador
description: Large hummingbird with limited range on west slope of Andes from central Colombia to northwest Ecuador. Distinctive in range.

name: Giant Ibis
rangeDescription: Lowlands of thailand, cambodia, laos, and southern vietnam
description: A hulking gray ibis the size of a large goose and with a distinctively long-bodied appearance, this increasingly rare scimitar-billed waterbird is unmistakable in its limited range. Size alone separates this species from other ibises that share its range; also note wrinkly bald head, dark back, and beautifully scalloped wings.

name: Mindoro Bulbul
rangeDescription: Philippines (mindoro and semirara)
description: A medium-sized bird of lowland and montane forest and more open wooded areas on Mindoro and Semirara. Dark brown on the upperparts and chest with a pale belly, a fairly long stout black bill, and a grayish head with faint streaks.

name: Black-crowned Palm-Tanager
rangeDescription: Lowlands of hispaniola (except southern peninsular haiti) incluidng saona island
description: A slow-moving and occasionally tail-twitching species of woodland thickets and dense cover; often found in mixed-species flocks. Note its black face and crown that is boldly marked with white spots and contrasts sharply with an entirely white throat.

name: Black-cheeked Mountain Tanager
rangeDescription: Santa marta mountains (northeastern colombia)
description: Large, colorful tanager found only in the Santa Marta Mountains of Colombia. Note the black mask, yellow dot behind eye, and azure crown; plumage is otherwise blue and yellow.

name: Zimmer's Tody-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Local in western amazonia (ecuador in pastaza; peru in eastern loreto); more widespread from northeastern bolivia across central and eastern amazonian brazil
description: Very small flycatcher with a long thin bill and yellow eyes. Brownish-olive above and olive-buff below with indistinct dusky streaks.

name: Levant Sparrowhawk
rangeDescription: Balkans to russia; winters to northeastern africa and arabian peninsula
description: Small, dark-eyed hawk of woodland, scrub, riparian corridors, and wooded plains and slopes. Note the adult's grayish upperparts and orange-barred underparts; females are larger and darker than males, with a dark central throat stripe.

name: Small-headed Elaenia
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (rio de janeiro) to eastern paraguay and northeastern argentina
description: Medium-sized flycatcher with a small head and long tail. Found in forests and second growth.

name: White-rumped Snowfinch
rangeDescription: Tibet to western china (kokonor and nan shan mountains to sichuan)
description: A frosty little finch with a black patch around the eye and bright white wing patches and tail edges. Forages in high-altitude meadows, pastures, and grasslands, as well as in towns and monasteries, around which it can often be quite tame.

name: Yellow-footed Honeyguide
rangeDescription: Sierra leone to liberia, southwestern ghana, and southwestern cameroon
description: Medium-sized honeyguide with a plain face, a slim pale bill, yellow legs, and large white patches in the outer tail. Found in the middle levels and canopy of humid forest at low and middle elevations.

name: Gray-striped Spurfowl
rangeDescription: Locally in escarpment of western angola
description: Large and brownish francolin that is endemic to Angola. Mostly buffy brown, with pale stripes on the back and chestnut stripes on the underparts.

name: Tibetan Sandgrouse
rangeDescription: Desert of eastern afghanistan to tibetan plateau
description: A sandy-colored ground bird with a thin needle-point tail and a gentle, dove-like profile. Not as well-marked as other sandgrouse: soft sandy brown with a light orange face and finely barred breast.

name: Baker's Imperial-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Banks group and northern vanuatu
description: A large, strikingly dark pigeon with an entirely dark upperside, a purple throat, a gray head, and a chestnut belly and underwing. Found mainly on large islands above 600 meters of elevation, but occasionally coastal.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Black-collared Swallow
rangeDescription: Rapids on rivers of the guianas, southern venezuela, and amazonian brazil
description: Small, handsome swallow of boulder-strewn rivers. Black-and-white pattern is distinctive but can be surprisingly hard to discern in bright sunlight.

name: Lilac-tailed Parrotlet
rangeDescription: Northern venezuela to trinidad and tobago and the guianas
description: Small parrot of rainforest regions. Generally uncommon; distinctive black-and green plumage and purple tail render it unmistakable on the rare occasions it is seen well.

name: Medium Tree-Finch
rangeDescription: Humid scrub of floreana (galapagos)
description: A critically endangered Galápagos finch found only on the island of Floreana. Bill is moderately curved on both upper and lower edges, and slightly longer than it is deep.

name: Alström's Warbler
rangeDescription: Western and southern china; winters to thailand, cambodia, and northern vietnam
description: Sprightly, small warbler that poses a bevy of identification issues. Dull olive above and yellow below, with a bright eyering and a gray crown bound in by black stripes.

name: Lesser Nothura
rangeDescription: Semiarid grassland and scrub of interior southeastern brazil and east-central paraguay
description: Sandy-colored tinamou that usually holds an upright posture. Has a brown crown and a heavily streaked back and throat.

name: White-capped Bunting
rangeDescription: Southern turkmenistan to northern afghanistan, northern pakistan and northwestern india
description: Male’s elegant black-and-white facial pattern is unique. Female is plain, streaky brown all over with faint white eye-ring, a weak hint of the male’s facial pattern, and a small white spot on the “ears”.

name: Horned Parakeet
rangeDescription: New caledonia
description: Spectacular, relatively large mostly green parakeet with blue on the tail and wings, black face, red crown, and thin but prominent “horns” consisting of a crest made up of a pair of black feathers. Found in remnant patches of high-quality forest.
